craft_claim: Cynical wit compresses the gap between professed motive and attributed motive into a portable counter-maxim; the unit works only where the professed ideal is shared enough to be recognized when inverted.

supporting_evidence.note: The echoic-reminder model makes the prior expectation the trigger of ironic access: the maxim form supplies that prior inside itself, restating the shared claim before overturning it in the same breath.

supporting_evidence.location: Introduction and the sequence of maxims on self-esteem, virtue, and friendship (Tancock trans.)
supporting_evidence.note: La Rochefoucauld's method re-describes admired motives — virtue, friendship, love, loyalty — as operations of self-love, producing deflation in a single portable sentence rather than an argument.
The maxim delivers the cynical insight as a quotable unit the reader can carry and redeploy against new cases; serial deflation accumulates from wit into worldview.

counterevidence.note: Section H item 1: ironic access requires a fresh recoverable prior, so a portable maxim that re-deflates an ideal already deflated teaches the reader to skip (section G 'Edgelord contrarianism': inversion without referent); the unit's portability is bounded by the stated claims present in the scene.

scope: Aphoristic prose, narrator asides, epigrammatic dialogue; anywhere a single sentence must carry the deflation.
exceptions: Where the audience does not share the ideal (subcultural or historical distance), the inversion reads as nonsense or aggression rather than recognition.
Maxim-form deflation carries no plot: in narrative it must be attached to a character, a target, or a stake, or it becomes wallpaper (see dosage claim).
